title: Your Guide to the Fadiman Microdosing Protocol
abstract:
**Overview**: Microdosing involves taking very low, sub-hallucinogenic doses of psychedelic substances, such as LSD or magic mushrooms, and has gained popularity in recent years. The Fadiman Microdosing Protocol, popularized by Dr. James Fadiman, suggests taking a microdose one day, two days off, and repeating. Anecdotal reports suggest benefits in mood, focus, and creativity, but formal research is limited. Recent systematic reviews and studies have provided some insights into the potential benefits of microdosing, but more rigorous scientific investigation is needed to fully understand its effects and risks. While some studies have reported positive effects on mental health, pain perception, and awareness, the lack of placebo-controlled studies limits our knowledge of microdosing and its effects. Care must be taken to avoid potential risks, such as taking more than intended. Further research, including double-blind placebo-controlled studies, is necessary to determine whether microdosing offers genuine benefits beyond the placebo effect.
[Microdosing](https://www.webdelics.com/explore-by-use-case/performance) is a novel approach to psychedelic usage that has garnered increasing attention in the Western world. As outlined by psychologist and psychedelic researcher Dr. James Fadiman in his 2011 work, ‘*The Psychedelic Explorer’s Guide: Safe, Therapeutic, and Sacred Journeys*’, microdosing refers to the practice of consuming very small, sub-perceptual doses of psychedelic substances such as LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide) or psilocybin-containing mushrooms (magic mushrooms). People who engage in microdosing often follow a specific schedule.  
The general idea behind microdosing is to experience the potential cognitive and creative benefits of psychedelics without the full-blown psychedelic effects. Proponents suggest that microdosing may lead to increased creativity, improved mood, enhanced focus, among other potential benefits. The intent is to potentially benefit from subtle, positive effects.  
While formal research on microdosing remains limited, Dr. Fadiman's exploration has been fueled by thousands of anecdotal reports from users. Many have reported experiencing benefits in mood enhancement, improved focus, heightened creativity, and enriched relationships. As information circulated through word-of-mouth and platforms like Reddit, the practice gained popularity, finding a niche in the competitive landscape of Silicon Valley.
A 2022 [review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0149763422001956?ref=pdf_download&fr=RR-2&rr=8302ea9fdc3e8675) of 44 studies on microdosing found evidence of its influence on pain perception, time perception, and awareness, with emerging indications of potential benefits for mental health, substance abuse disorders, and psychological functioning.  
However, a recent placebo-controlled [study](https://www.webdelics.com/post/home-administered-lsd-microdosing-study-short-term-mood-boosting-effects-but-no-significant-long-term-benefits) with 80 participants (40 receiving LSD) observed short-term mood-boosting effects but found no significant long-term benefits, as the positive effects did not extend beyond the trial duration.  
To summarize, the Fadiman Microdosing Protocol, proposed by psychologist Dr. James Fadiman, involves regularly taking very low doses of psychedelic substances like LSD or magic mushrooms on a fixed schedule.  
Typically, individuals administer 5%-10% of a standard psychedelic dose, such as 10-20 micrograms of LSD or 0.1 to 0.3 grams of dried psilocybin mushrooms. The protocol suggests a regimen where users take a microdose on the first day, abstain for the next two days, and then repeat the cycle.
